coverage: Pier & Point covers four sites on San Francisco's central waterfront: Mission Rock, Mission Bay, Pier 70 and Potrero Power Station. A parcel that is not in this data is outside coverage, not "no activity".

record.name: Pier 70 Waterfront Open Space
names: Pier 70 Waterfront Open Space (Waterfront Terrace / Slipways Commons / Waterfront Promenade / Pier 70 Shoreline)
record.summary: The roughly five-acre waterfront park system of the Pier 70 D4D (Waterfront Terrace, Slipways Commons and Waterfront Promenade, Sections 3.5-3.7) plus the roughly 1,300-foot Pier 70 Shoreline (Section 3.8), to be built by the developer and owned by the Port. Phase 1 includes three acres of parks, but the DDA ties park completion to adjacent buildings and the Port's 2026 report says the balance of Phase 1, 'largely comprised of the Phase 1 parks and open space, will be constructed on a schedule that coincides with the delivery of adjacent vertical development' and that 'construction of Phase 1 vertical projects and parks has not moved forward', so none has been constructed. The Port Commission heard that report at an informational hearing on August 11, 2026 (no action taken); it proposes amendments, not yet adopted, to 'better align open spaces with revised vertical development schedule'.

notes.accuracy_caveat: The outline is the union of Assessor lots 4052003, 4116001, 4116003 and 4116007, so its edges are recorded lot lines, not a trace. The lots are Pier & Point's reading of the plan diagram and the satellite imagery: 4052003 is zone 1 (Waterfront Terrace), 4116001 is zone 2 (Slipways Commons), and 4116003 and 4116007 are parts of zone 3 (Waterfront Promenade). No document read names these lots. Zone 4 (Pier 70 Shoreline) has no lot assigned and is not drawn, and the Port's SUD Land Use Plan splits these spaces into separate open space segments that this combined outline does not follow. The lots are the legal boundaries and may not follow the D4D's drawn edges. The open space is planned (Port Item 11A, memo dated Aug 7, 2026: the balance of Phase 1, largely the Phase 1 parks and open space, will be built on a schedule that coincides with adjacent vertical development). Lot 4175028 (21,885 m2, DataSF, Delaware St) was also proposed for zone 3 but is not used: it covers Potrero Power Station Blocks 3, 4 and 9 and other Potrero shapes, and Pier & Point has deferred it to the review of the Potrero Power Station site.
notes.digitized_from: DataSF Assessor parcels (acdm-wktn), lots 4052003, 4116001, 4116003 and 4116007 (recorded 2019-02-07; mapped 2019-03-14; active), joined into one outline; cross-checked against Pier 70 Design for Development Figure 6.4.2 - Building Height Maximum (p.155) and Figure 3.4.1 (Overview of Public Spaces, p.52).
notes.why_no_real_parcel: No document names the Assessor lots of the waterfront open space. Lots 4052003, 4116001, 4116003 and 4116007 (active) were assigned to its zones 1, 2 and 3 from Pier & Point's reading of the plan diagram, so its outline is their union.
notes.regulatory_context: Part of the Pier 70 D4D's Open Space Network (Section 3) -- specifically Sections 3.5 (Waterfront Terrace), 3.6 (Slipways Commons), 3.7 (Waterfront Promenade), and 3.8 (Pier 70 Shoreline, ~1,300 linear feet). Together with Building 12 Plaza/Market Square, 20th Street Plaza, Irish Hill Corner Plaza, and Irish Hill Playground, these comprise the D4D's total nine acres of public open space (Section 3.4).

The Port's 2017 staff report (Item 9B, p.7) puts the Schedule of Performance in the Disposition and Development Agreement (DDA) between the Port and the developer, which is a different agreement from the Development Agreement between the City and the developer. open_questions: No Port Commission schematic-design approval for any of the four waterfront open spaces was found on 2018-2026 agendas, so none appears to have reached that stage.
Which named spaces make up the three Phase 1 acres is not stated; the reading of Exhibit A above (Slipways Commons area in Phase 1) is this project's interpretation of a diagram.

Cost of the parks: the 2017 memo gives $260.5 million of eligible horizontal costs for all three phases but no park line item was extracted; the Port and developer's June 2025 project update says of November 2022 'Received NOC from City on the Phase 1 infrastructure' and 'Represented $150m investment' (NOC is the deck's abbreviation, read here as Notice of Completion), without a park breakdown.

Interim use: the Elevation Sky Park venue is planned as a five-year interim use ('DURATION: Period of 5 years', community engagement deck, June 25, 2025) on 'Phase 2/3 sites within Pier 70 development zone, away from waterfront buffer zone', and the Port's Executive Director described its location as 'where that street [22nd Street] meets the Bay' (Port Commission minutes, July 8, 2025); whether any of it sits on future park land or only on parcels E3/H2 is unresolved (see the E3 record).

Whether the hosted photograph qualifies as a 'before' view (taken within two years of construction starting) cannot be checked because no construction start is dated for this record; Wikimedia Commons titles it only 'Old shipyard building at Pier 70', and that its foreground is the future open space is our reading of the camera position.
